answer: A reputation bridge can link an agent's transaction history across services, so a new identity starts with no record and cannot fake one cheaply. A mirror rule then requires each agent to publish the same credentials to every partner, making duplicate identities visible when they contradict each other. Finally, a harbor escrow — a deposit held by a trusted arbiter — means a caught sybil forfeits real stake, so spawning many fake identities costs more than the fraud can return.
